mutants.reason: The || to && change only matters for WRAP bursts with an illegal length (not 2/4/8/16) or an address not aligned to the size. Both are AXI-illegal. The plan's assumptions say they are never generated and no rule defines the response. For legal WRAP both terms are 0, so the result is the same.

The AW context (ID, address, len, size, burst, prot, error flag) would be captured whenever the FSM is not IDLE, and never at the AW handshake. BID, PADDR, PPROT and the unsupported-write decision would be wrong.
WREADY would default to 1 in IDLE, REQ, WAIT and BRESP. W beats would be accepted before AW and while an APB beat is in flight, and without being captured.

In REQ the APB FSM is always IDLE and the grant is held, so i_req_ready is 1 in the first REQ cycle. The mutant stays in REQ one extra cycle, until the APB FSM reaches SETUP and req_ready drops to 0. Then it moves to WAIT. The earliest rsp_valid comes two cycles after that, so WAIT is entered in time. The APB transfer and every other output are unchanged, and the extra o_req_valid cycle is ignored by the APB FSM.
The WRAP next-address decision is inverted. Beats that should wrap would increment, and beats that should increment would jump to the wrap base. APB addresses for legal WRAP writes would be wrong.

req_ready would be asserted only while the APB FSM is not IDLE. The request would never be captured in IDLE, and the sequencers would see ready in the wrong phase. The APB transfer would be corrupted or never run.

The response pulse (rd/wr rsp_valid, data, err) would fire outside the ACCESS state whenever PREADY is high. It would not fire at the real completion, so read data, PSLVERR and B/R timing would be wrong or the bridge would hang.

reg_wr_err would be set whenever the sticky registered rsp_err is 1, in any state, not only at a WAIT completion with PSLVERR. A write error would leak into the following error-free write, which would return SLVERR in BRESP.

This is a default assignment in p_com_outputs. The following case on the APB state has SETUP, ACCESS and a default branch, and each branch assigns o_apb_pwrite. The default value is always overwritten, so the port never changes.
w_ar_valid is never set back to 1. Every read, including legal ones, would be treated as unsupported. It would get SLVERR beats with no APB access.
A captured write would set reg_apb_wr=0. PWRITE would be 0 on writes, so they would be issued as APB reads. The completion would also be routed to the read response path, so no B would be returned.
ARREADY would default to 1 outside IDLE and without a grant. A new AR could be accepted while a transaction is active, or when the read side is not granted.
The state cannot equal both WDAT and DRAIN. WREADY would never be asserted, so no W beat is accepted and every write hangs.

i_rd_done can only be 1 while the controller is in ACTRD. In the mutant, reg_turn_rd clears to 0 at the start of ACTRD instead of at its end. reg_turn_rd is only read in controller IDLE, and the only exit from ACTRD is rd_done, which sets the same value. The tie-break order is identical.
The APB FSM would need both a read request and a write request at once to leave IDLE. That can never happen, so no APB transfer would start.
The 4-KiB crossing flag is inverted. Reads that cross 4 KiB would be accepted and issue APB traffic, and non-crossing legal reads would be rejected with SLVERR.
RVALID would be high in every state except RESP, including IDLE, reset, REQ and WAIT. It would be low in RESP. Spurious R beats would appear and the real beat would never be presented.
The forced zero data and SLVERR would apply in every state except ERR. Unsupported reads would return stored data and resp instead of zero and SLVERR, and legal beats would be forced to SLVERR.

beats_left and the address would advance whenever RESP/ERR is active even with RREADY low. They would also advance in non-R states when RREADY is high. The beat count, RLAST position and held R payload would be wrong.
o_wr_done would never be asserted. The controller would stay in ACTWR forever, the arbitration preference would never flip, and no further transaction would be accepted.
The state cannot be both RESP and ERR. RVALID would never be asserted, so no R beat would be returned and reads would hang.
o_req_valid would be asserted in every state except REQ. The APB FSM could start spurious transfers (including for unsupported writes), and in REQ the request would never be raised.
AWREADY would default to 1 outside IDLE and without a grant. A new AW could be accepted while a transaction is active, or when the write side is not granted.
The WAIT state would advance when no APB response is valid. It would advance before the APB completion, with wrong beat counting and address advance, and would miss the real response pulse.
The WRAP alignment check is inverted. Legal aligned WRAP writes would be rejected as unsupported, with SLVERR and no APB. Misaligned ones would be accepted.
The tie-break preference is inverted. The first tie after reset would go to AW, and later ties would favour the side just served. Lone requests are still granted.
o_rd_req_ready is only 1 in APB IDLE, so the read capture branch would never run. APB read address, PPROT and PWRITE would not be loaded and would keep stale values.
W data would be captured and beats_left decremented whenever WVALID is high in any state, or whenever the state is WDAT without WVALID. PWDATA, PSTRB and the beat count would be corrupted.
PENABLE would be 1 in the idle/default APB state with PSEL=0. It would be asserted without PSEL, including after reset.
A WRAP burst with ARLEN=7 (8 beats) would be treated as an invalid length. Legal 8-beat WRAP reads would be rejected with SLVERR and no APB.
PSEL would be 0 during ACCESS while PENABLE=1. The APB access phase would be illegal and the completer would not see a selected access.
The INCR beat count would be inflated by 256. The 4-KiB crossing check would flag legal INCR reads near the end of a page, rejecting them with SLVERR and no APB.

The || to && change only matters for WRAP writes with an illegal length or an unaligned address. Both are AXI-illegal. The plan's assumptions say they are never generated and no rule defines the response. For legal WRAP both terms are 0, so the result is the same.

An APB transfer would start whenever o_gnt_rd is high, even without a valid read request. Extra APB transfers would appear, including for unsupported reads, and the transfer count would exceed ARLEN+1.
The WRAP next-address decision for reads is inverted. Wrapping bursts would increment past the boundary instead of wrapping, and non-wrapping beats would jump to the wrap base.
RLAST would be inverted. It would be high on every beat except the last and low on the final beat. The transaction would never complete correctly.
